tickets.title: Expand the engine with an input and character-rule seam while preserving byte behavior
tickets.problem: The current VM and parser encode byte/classic-C assumptions. Unicode and platform rules need a shared mechanism without replacing the byte path in one broad refactor.
tickets.current_state: The paused byte graph/typed-unwind implementation exists; no generic input or production traits seam has independent acceptance.
deliverables: Introduce internal cursor/input-unit and character-rule interfaces beside the current byte entry points. Route one complete classic-C byte compile/search/capture path through them.
Record original backstop, search start, attempt start, previous context and public-unit conversion invariants. Preserve the old public path until adapters have parity.
acceptance: The frozen checkpoint and the expanded path produce identical complete results on the same predeclared byte corpus, including NUL, arbitrary bytes, partial extents and histories. This preserves current behavior and does not close the separate B-series Boost compatibility obligations.
No Unicode normalization, UTF-8 requirement or changed byte error position is introduced.
The architecture document identifies the remaining migration batches and the eventual contract/removal gate.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Implement the UTF-32 Unicode compile, search and capture adapter
tickets.problem: Unicode execution must consume original u32 units while using the pinned ICU character rules.
tickets.current_state: The sorting research CLI accepts UTF-32; the production regex API does not.
deliverables: Connect the shared parser/VM and fixed Unicode rules to UTF-32 pattern and input APIs, with result ranges and errors measured in original u32 units.
Implement upstream acceptance/rejection of out-of-range values and surrogates at the correct operation boundary; retain literal NUL.
acceptance: Native Boost u32 regex cases compare status, category, position, complete captures and histories for valid, malformed, supplementary and NUL inputs.
Pattern decoding errors and input traversal errors retain their separate source-defined locations.
Public documentation includes an executable UTF-32 search/capture example.

Boost icu.hpp passes 4-byte regex iterators directly while 1/2-byte entry points decode; do not impose sort-key UTF-32-to-UTF-16 input rejection on the distinct regex API without source and native evidence.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Implement UTF-16 decoding and original-unit regex positions
tickets.problem: A scalar cursor must preserve surrogate-pair and lone-surrogate behavior and UTF-16 public offsets.
tickets.current_state: Sort-key input decoding exists only in the research tool; no accepted regex adapter exists.
deliverables: Add UTF-16 pattern/input cursors and public compile/search/full-match operations over the shared Unicode engine.
Keep forward/backward traversal, lookbehind and partial extents in original UTF-16 units.
acceptance: Compare full results and errors with Boost for every surrogate boundary class, supplementary matches, malformed patterns, malformed input, NUL and empty input.
Lookbehind, captures and search subranges retain exact original u16 offsets; no replacement-character repair or prenormalization occurs.
The same logical valid text agrees with UTF-32 semantic results after explicit independently checked unit mapping.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Implement UTF-8 Unicode regex APIs without losing original byte positions
tickets.problem: Unicode UTF-8 and arbitrary-byte regex are different APIs, and internal scalar positions must never leak.
tickets.current_state: Byte APIs accept arbitrary bytes; production Unicode UTF-8 regex entry points are missing.
deliverables: Add UTF-8 pattern/input cursors and safe Unicode compile/search/full-match entry points.
Preserve upstream forward/backward decoding behavior, invalid UTF-8 errors, previous context and original byte ranges.
acceptance: Compare full results and error categories/positions for overlong, truncated, stray-continuation, surrogate and above-maximum encodings plus valid 1–4 byte sequences.
Capture histories, lookbehind, partial matches and range searches report exact byte offsets into the original input.
An invalid UTF-8 byte sequence remains usable by the distinct byte API.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Expand native-wide input and positions through deterministic character rules
tickets.problem: Native wchar behavior follows the platform traits and width; it is not automatically identical to ICU Unicode mode.
tickets.current_state: The current public engine is byte-only.
deliverables: Expose native-wide compile/search/capture entry points through deterministic custom rules and the shared engine before wiring production platform backends. Preserve Windows 16-bit and Unix native 32-bit units and representation.
Keep native-wide, ICU UTF-16 and ICU UTF-32 semantics distinct. Backend integrations N03–N08/N11–N12 follow this seam; I10 is the contract/removal gate.
acceptance: A deterministic custom-traits Boost reference and Rust tracer agree for wide compilation, matching, captures, NUL, code-unit boundaries and original ranges without depending on a completed native locale backend.
The API preserves each platform native unit representation and source-defined input domain; no global Unicode validation/repair policy is imposed.
The seam supports native C/C++/Win32 backends without implementing them in this ticket, and a public example exercises the full tracer.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: only the native-wide input seam, deterministic rule tracer, public positions and focused differential fixtures; each production backend has its own ticket.

deliverables: Reuse accepted formatter and iteration mechanisms through encoding-aware input/output sinks. Preserve captures, callback views, replacement bytes/units and input consumption.

acceptance: Complete native-reference results agree for empty progress, multiple groups, trailing unmatched input, conditional formats, callbacks and malformed input boundaries in each adapter.
Output and all ranges remain in the original input/output unit types; explicit sink failures obey ADR-0003.
Executable examples show each encoding using the same semantic operations.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: migrate only the UTF-32 high-level operations to the accepted generic formatter/iteration mechanism.

tickets.title: Specify and implement independent compile-work and compile-memory limits
tickets.problem: ADR-0003 permits independent necessary limits but requires precise errors and documented accounting; research budget proposals are not accepted defaults.
tickets.current_state: The paused engine has provisional Limits fields and counters, without a complete public accounting contract or retained boundary evidence.
deliverables: Document which parser/compiler operations and owned capacities are charged, allocation failure handling and default necessary engine limits.
Implement explicit compile-budget configuration and error propagation without changing ordinary pattern errors or adopting unconfirmed research values as requirements.
acceptance: Boundary-minus-one, boundary and boundary-plus-one tests cover parsing, groups, ranges, recursion analysis and instruction/data allocation.
Limit rejection is an explicit resource error; a valid empty regex or no-match is never substituted.
Default calls add no output cap or traversal-total budget, and confirmed error category/position behavior stays unchanged.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Implement execution-work and engine-memory budget accounting
tickets.problem: Typed rollback, recursion and retained histories need coherent budget accounting across every execution scope.
tickets.current_state: Current counters and 35 local tests do not prove complete resource behavior or memory acceptance.
deliverables: Charge the defined units across search attempts, recursion, assertions, single-state repeats and capture-history allocation.
Expose opt-in execution accounting with deterministic errors and preserve the independent-resource compatibility boundary.
acceptance: Budget boundaries cover each allocation/transition family and nested scopes; failures never become successful truncated captures or no-match.
Default behavior does not acquire an unapproved cumulative traversal budget.
Compare native-reference resource failures separately from semantic differences; a Rust success within its budget is permitted and identified under ADR-0003.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Implement explicit output and match-count budgets for high-level operations
tickets.problem: Requested budgets need a documented counting scope without changing the default output/iteration contract.

deliverables: Define and implement explicit caller-selected output-byte/unit, match-count and optional cumulative-work budget scope across replace, collect and traversal operations.
Keep compile budgets separate and make all counters checked for overflow.
acceptance: Default operations impose no newly added output or total-traversal cap.
Opt-in limits count the documented units and lifecycle consistently across multiple matches and callbacks.
All-at-once APIs return an error on exhaustion and never return a success-shaped truncated value; boundary cases and counter overflow are tested.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.

tickets.title: Preserve streaming output and terminal iterator errors on exhaustion
tickets.problem: Streaming consumers can already have observed output or matches when a budget or sink fails.
tickets.current_state: Only initial byte iterator/replacement operations exist; error-once and written-prefix semantics are not accepted.
deliverables: Apply limits and sink errors to write-to, callback and iterator APIs using a terminal error state.
Preserve previously returned items and already written output, and keep internal results independent between invocations.
acceptance: An iterator returns every previously delivered match, exactly one error at exhaustion, then permanent end including repeated next calls.
An external sink retains precisely its written prefix when an error is reported; no rollback is promised.
One-shot, iterator and streaming tests exercise the same failure points and demonstrate their deliberately different result-delivery contracts.
tickets.sizing: One fresh context: implement and verify only the named input adapter, backend, or budget mechanism; reuse the independently accepted engine and do not combine other backends.
